exposure: Infants with an adverse outcome were compared to all spontaneous singleton vaginal breech deliveries with normal perinatal and neonatal outcomes.
cohort: 786 singleton term breech deliveries with a planned vaginal delivery
finding: A second delivery stage lasting <40 minutes was associated with lower odds of adverse neonatal outcomes, while epidural anesthesia was associated with higher adverse outcomes.
mod_finding: This study found that a prolonged second stage of labor lasting >40 minutes during a vaginal breech delivery was associated with adverse neonatal outcomes, while epidural anesthesia was associated with higher adverse outcomes.
